expected.name: Bertha Wallerstein
expected.description:
Bertha Wallerstein was a member of the National Woman's Party and one of the "Silent Sentinels" imprisoned during the 1917-1919 campaign to picket the Wilson White House for woman suffrage. (Recorded as Bertha "Betsy" Wallerstein Hutchison; May 25, 1899 - July 3, 1950)

She was arrested on February 4, 1919, though the disposition of that arrest is unresolved. Arrested again at the watchfire demonstration of February 9, she was sentenced the following day to five days and released on February 13.

Her jail term was in February 1919, not January; earlier versions of this record placed it in the wrong month.

updates.body:
Photo credit

Barnard College, Mortarboard, volume 26 (1920 yearbook, published 1919), page 166. Mechanical scan crop via Wikimedia Commons; public-domain original. Downloaded unchanged; 201 by 243 pixels. Source photograph.

operations.name: Patreese Johnson

expected.charges: Gang assault, attempted assault (self-defense against street harasser)
expected.sentence: Originally sentenced to 11 years in prison on June 14, 2007; reduced on appeal to eight years, with five years of post-release supervision. Johnson retrospectively confirmed she returned home in August 2013. The exact release day and complete custody chronology remain unverified.

operations.source: https://www.salon.com/2014/08/18/we_thought_wed_be_safe_islan_nettles_the_new_jersey_4_and_the_illusion_of_security_for_lgbtq_people_of_color/ — identifies Johnson among the four who pleaded not guilty. Crucial custody qualification: the original documentary press kit, https://www.thefilmcollaborative.org/films/img/epk/Press_Kit_Out_In_The_Night_052814.pdf page 6, records Patreese being bailed out in September 2006. Initial arrest therefore cannot begin an uninterrupted seven-year interval. Existing partial release and missing admission remain unchanged.

expected.name: Herb Powless
expected.description: Oneida AIM leader and founder of the Milwaukee chapter of the American Indian Movement, imprisoned at the federal penitentiary in Terre Haute, Indiana in the 1970s on weapons-related charges that supporters tied to government targeting of AIM organizers. Documented in PFOC Breakthrough magazine.

updates.body:
Photo credit

Jack Siebold, MyTown report on the fortieth anniversary of Wounded Knee, February 27, 2013. Caption explicitly identifies Herb Powless. Original web portrait downloaded unchanged, 164 by 168 pixels. Copyright retained by the photographer; no open license or permission claimed. Used for educational biographical identification at the site owner’s direction. Source photograph.

operations.name: Robert Lee Hill

updates.sentence: Held for months in Topeka while extradition and federal charges were contested. Kansas Governor Henry J. Allen refused extradition in March 1920; federal charges were dismissed in October 1920. No imposed custodial sentence is established by this source.

operations.source: https://encyclopediaofarkansas.net/entries/robert-lee-hill-3026/ — Robert Lee Hill entry by John Gruber, updated July 20, 2026. Distinguishes pretrial detention, refused extradition and dismissal; does not characterize months detained as a judicial sentence. All populated dates and biography preserved.

operations.name: Miguel Alcudia Gamas

expected.name: Miguel Alcudia Gamas
expected.description: Miguel Alcudia Gamas is a Migrant Justice farmworker organizer detained by ICE on September 22, 2016. A federal complaint alleged that officers used Vermont motor-vehicle records to target him and warned that another organizer would be next. Migrant Justice's October 14, 2016 update reports that he was released the previous night, October 13, after ICE waived his bond. Release ended this detention, not his immigration proceedings. This is a historical custody outcome, not a claim about his present immigration status.
expected.body:
Case history and verification

Miguel Alcudia Gamas is a Migrant Justice member detained by ICE on September 22, 2016. A federal complaint alleged that officers used Vermont motor-vehicle records to target him and warned that another organizer would be next. He was named among the plaintiffs in the group's retaliation litigation. The reviewed sources establish historical detention but do not establish a release date or present custody status; he is not flagged as currently detained.

Status reviewed October 8, 2026: Historical detention established. Present custody and release date unconfirmed; current-custody flag is not asserted.

Sources

  • Federal complaint, paragraphs 60–68
  • CCR: named clients and case history

Verified detail sources (October 8, 2026): The November 14, 2018 Migrant Justice complaint, paragraph 13, provides the named plaintiff’s biography and explicitly uses he/him. The identity matches the existing Vermont organizing and detention case. Source 1.

Release and photograph verified October 12, 2026: Migrant Justice's update dated October 14, 2016 reports Miguel's actual release the previous night, establishing October 13, 2016 (21 elapsed days after September 22). ICE waived the bond; proceedings continued. This supersedes the older release-unconfirmed note. The unaltered original campaign photograph on that same named petition identifies Miguel; credit Migrant Justice, photographer unspecified, no open-license claim.

operations.source: https://www.acluvt.org/sites/default/files/field_documents/2017-10-11_complaint.pdf paragraph 18 identifies full name Miguel Alfredo Alcudia Gamas and September 22, 2016 ICE arrest; the 2018 complaint identifies the same organizer as Miguel Alcudia Gamas. Add alternate full name only; no criminal conviction or sentence inferred.
